# [TASK] Terraform: AWS free-tier infrastructure (k3s on EC2 t3.small)

## Task
Provision the secondary cloud target per ARCHITECTURE.md §11.2: single-node k3s on an EC2 instance (EKS's managed control plane is not free, ~$73/month).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Remote state (S3 bucket `filmpire-tfstate-4288` + DynamoDB lock table `filmpire-tfstate-lock`) bootstrapped live against a real AWS account
      (`terraform -chdir=infrastructure/terraform/aws validate`)
- [x] `modules/network-aws`, `modules/cluster-k3s` (t3.small + k3s user_data, 30GB root volume), `modules/budget-guard-aws` — apply/destroy round-trip with zero manual console steps beyond one-time IAM user creation
      (`terraform -chdir=infrastructure/terraform/aws validate`)
- [x] Core service slice runs on the single node, gateway reachable end-to-end — real TMDB data flowing gateway -> movie-service -> MongoDB -> Redis -> gateway; `terraform destroy` confirmed clean (both instances terminated, no VPCs/budgets left)
- [x] Runs within AWS free credits, budget-guard tripwire live — `t3.micro` OOM-thrashes under this app's real footprint (load average 15+ on 2 vCPUs, <70MiB free) and `t3.medium` is blocked outright on this account; `t3.small` is the smallest size that actually stays up, a small real hourly cost covered by free credits — same "free" definition as #26
- [x] Credentials via `AWS_*` env vars, live-tested with a real IAM user (`terraform-filmpire`, AdministratorAccess); GitHub OIDC federated role documented but not yet wired into CI

## Estimate
**Hours:** 16

## Notes
- Resizing/restarting the node in place breaks k3s's advertised IP (`user_data` only runs on first boot, so a later restart leaves a stale `--node-external-ip`) — no durable fix yet; destroy and recreate instead of resizing.
- Not wired into `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml` (Azure-only currently).
- Images for this live run were pushed manually — `docker-publish.yml` (#28) wasn't firing yet at the time.

Reference: ARCHITECTURE.md §11.1–11.2
